item.title: Democrats’ blue wave beat Texas’ GOP gerrymanders. Did California even need Prop. 50?
item.description:
In summary Democrats notched big wins across the country, even in deep red districts that Republicans in Texas, Florida and North Carolina had gerrymandered to benefit their own party. That begs the question — did California really need to toss aside its independent redistricting commission? California Democrats went all in on redistricting last year in a rebuke of President Donald Trump’s call for Republicans to gerrymander red states and preserve their U.S. House majority. Ultimately, though, it appears such a gamble wasn’t even necessary. The “blue tsunami” that engulfed the country was enough to sweep away Republicans in ruby-red districts that Trump won by double digits two years ago as Democrats improved on their 2024 margin by a stunning 15 percentage points. item.title: NASA's Swift space telescope plunges back to Earth in fiery demise
item.description:
NASA One of NASA’s leading space telescopes crashed down to Earth on Wednesday, less than three months after a last-ditch rescue mission failed. The Swift Observatory reentered Earth’s atmosphere at 7:39 a.m. ET over Indonesia’s North Sumatra region. Intense solar activity over the last few years dragged its orbit down. It is not yet clear how much of the 1.5-ton spacecraft burned up in the atmosphere. NASA said much of it did, though some components were expected to survive. It has not been confirmed whether any debris reached the ground. According to NASA, the odds of the debris harming anyone were about one in 2,100. Private company Katalyst Space had been hired to boost the telescope’s orbit. The company’s robotic craft launched in July but ran into trouble soon after, and it crashed back to Earth in September. item.title: Trump Scrambles to Halt Military Aid to Israel to Deprive El-Sayed of a Talking Point
item.description:
The United States will stop providing $4 billion in annual aid to Israel starting next year, President Donald Trump claimed in an Election Day interview. While the U.S. will continue to sell arms to its closest Middle East ally, Trump’s announcement — should it actually hold true — could represent a seismic shift in American foreign policy. Still questions remain and experts are dubious that the claim is what it seems. Trump told Fox News during a phone call on Tuesday that Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu had approached him with the idea years ago. He did not state specifically why he waited to announce the decision in the midst of a midterm vote in which his party is expected to lose its lock on Congress , but noted that U.S. aid to Israel has become a Democratic talking point, singling out Michigan Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed. “The left uses the $4 billion payment — that…
